**Group:** Ciliates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A fusiform (spindle shaped) naked ciliate (ie aloricate) with an apical mouth region and many longitudinal rows of cilia (kineties) running the length of a fairly rigid pellicle (often not resolved with planktivore), which often gives a finely striped appearance. Key features: tapered spindle outline (fusiform), lengthwise ciliary rows, a single motile cell with no lorica.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **tintinnid** | Tintinnids sit inside an external lorica (shell); Tiarina is a naked spindle-shaped cell with no lorica. |
| **phaeocystis** | Phaeocystis is a gelatinous colony of many small non-ciliated cells; Tiarina is a single ciliated cell. |
